The basis is smaller and sound, the manufactured-evidence path is gone, the reader reports its own clause unmet rather than rebinding to make the number read ten, and it says out loud what it trusts. findings_the_fifth_reading_added: W5-F1 (material): reintroducing the exact title-reading defect this branch repaired left selfcheck at exit 0, because every fixture stub's title carried its own term, so the mispaired stub read `unrelated` and a title-reading reader refused it for the right verdict by the wrong rule. The gate could not see the branch's headline repair while fixture.py said it could. Repaired: stub titles name no primitive, and primitive-mispaired carries a title naming the term it is not paired with, so a title-reading reader fails selfcheck by name.

W5-F2 (material): the new live-split test asserted that no reported entry contained "is governed by", a string the reported branch never writes. It could not fail. Replaced with one that rebuilds the governed set from PRIMITIVES and checks no reported closure sits in a contract a primitive names; it fails under the direct inverse of the repair.

W5-F5 (observation): the declaration rule was a denylist, and a properties dict inside an examples array was harvested as a declaration, which contradicted the module's own root-only reasoning. examples, example and fixtures are excluded now, and a root identifier carrying whitespace is not read as an identifier.

W5-F6 (observation): the closure scan read contracts/** only, so a primitive governed by a contract under services/ would be missed. Found while still vacuous and closed anyway; the scan is now contracts/** plus every .json a bound primitive names.

W5-F8 (method, not a finding against the work): verify.py exits 1 against a git archive copy because parts of it need .git. The fifth reading established that as its own copy's defect before recording.
